question: Can visually identical attention-sink stripes be separated into adaptive no-op and content-broadcast computations using residual-stream diagnostics, and do gating plus register tokens improve representations by addressing the two mechanisms complementarily?

key_findings.claim: Author framing: a sink can implement either an adaptive no-op or a broadcast, so attention mass alone is computationally ambiguous.
key_findings.evidence: In the no-op hypothesis, a query routes to a sink with negligible value contribution so the residual update is approximately zero. In the broadcast hypothesis, many queries retrieve a contentful sink value and receive a shared residual component. Both cases produce the same vertical stripe in an attention map but imply different interventions.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported toy result: the designed conditional-damping task learns a dedicated low-value sink and a dominant query-key singular direction, with sink formation persisting under partial damping and rarer no-op conditions.
key_findings.evidence: The one-head, width-64, length-32 pre-norm task explicitly supplies learned positional embeddings and a learned BOS offset, and asks the attention branch to reproduce each unmasked token but output a damped or zero copy for masked tokens. The displayed training trajectories select one near-zero-value position and a spectral spike; the damping and activation-frequency sweeps preserve sink formation. The paper does not state the number of independent toy runs, numerical endpoint values, or variability beyond plotted bands, so the evidence supports feasibility in this constructed task rather than a general optimization law.

anchors.section: 3.1 Toy Model of Adaptive NOP and Figure 2

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the finite-epsilon no-op lemma does not establish its stated two-solution dichotomy or value-norm bound, although the perfect-sink zero-output limit is valid.
key_findings.evidence: For an epsilon-sink the appendix writes o_i=(1-epsilon_i)v_s+r_i with ||r_i||<=epsilon V_max. From ||o_i||<=delta, reverse triangle gives at best ||v_s||<=(delta+epsilon V_max)/(1-epsilon_i), not the stated delta+epsilon V_max. Setting v_s approximately zero only guarantees ||o_i||<=epsilon V_max, which need not meet delta. Conversely, choosing v_s=-r_i/(1-epsilon_i) separately for each query does not produce one shared sink value unless all query residuals agree. Thus the proof neither proves the advertised exhaustive dichotomy nor its finite-epsilon inequality; only when epsilon tends to zero does o_i tend to v_s and a zero-tolerance no-op force v_s=0.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the adaptivity lemma supplies a sufficient rank-one construction and a product condition, not an exhaustive either-spectral-spike-or-massive-activation theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The proof assumes Theta=sigma uu^T and x_s=gamma_s u, yielding a sink logit proportional to lambda_i sigma gamma_s and the requirement sigma gamma_s much larger than a margin term. This shows that increasing either factor can help within the chosen construction, but it does not prove that every learned hard gate must use that rank-one alignment, that only one factor becomes large, or that other input/key geometry and competing logits cannot implement routing. The empirical spectral spike remains a reported signature of the toy run, while the claimed two-regime necessity is unproved.

key_findings.claim: Author theory and toy result: sink-dominated attention produces an approximately rank-one update, and a two-layer global-communication task learns a specialized contentful broadcast layer.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma 3 writes the head output as the outer product of sink attention weights and the sink value plus a residual bounded by the nonsink mass. On the Gaussian task, every token must add a rotated version of a selected source token; training assigns one layer to select and distribute that source, retains sink value norms around the content-token scale, collapses query-key geometry toward a routing direction, and reports stable rank near one for the broadcast update while the second layer remains more position-specific.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported pretrained phenomenology: DINOv2 and OpenCLIP move sink mass from CLS in early layers to patches in deeper layers, and sink behavior is concentrated in specialized heads.
key_findings.evidence: Attention-inflow plots for DINOv2-L, DINOv2-G, and OpenCLIP-L/16 show the layerwise handoff, while the DINOv2-L head map contains heads acting as sinks on nearly 80% of inputs next to heads that do not. Appendix figures report analogous handoffs or head specialization for EVA-G and OpenAI CLIP-L.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported diagnostic split: detected DINOv2-G sinks form a low-value-norm mode labeled no-op and a content-scale-value, rank-one mode labeled broadcast; similar plots are shown for EVA-G and OpenAI CLIP-L.
key_findings.evidence: The first DINOv2-G mode occurs mainly in early-to-middle layers and has sink value-norm ratios below 0.2. The second occurs deeper and combines ordinary value norms with near-rank-one attention updates. The appendix presents visually similar dual modes in EVA-G and OpenAI CLIP-L, but provides plots rather than a labeled quantitative benchmark or uncertainty analysis.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported register result: DINOv2-G register tokens absorb most detected sink mass but themselves exhibit both low-value and contentful rank-one modes.
key_findings.evidence: With four trained registers, patch and CLS sink assignments largely move to registers. Most register sinks have value-norm ratios below 0.2, while a smaller group has ratios near one and rank-one updates. The authors interpret this as register tokens being repurposed for no-op as well as their intended workspace role.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported mitigation result: every tested gating/register LeJEPA variant improves frozen-backbone dense linear probes over baseline, the two combined variants are strongest, and ImageNet online linear classification remains tightly clustered.
key_findings.evidence: Across three ViT-L backbones per variant, baseline ADE20K/VOC12 mIoU is 0.166±0.006/0.438±0.016; registers reach 0.187±0.002/0.499±0.001; elementwise gating 0.186±0.004/0.480±0.002; headwise gating 0.185±0.0003/0.476±0.006; elementwise plus registers 0.200±0.006/0.522±0.017; and headwise plus registers 0.199±0.003/0.524±0.013. ImageNet means span 69.07%-69.52%. No statistical test is supplied, and the best ADE20K and VOC12 means belong to different combined architectures.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: Lemma 4 is titled and interpreted as increased token similarity, but its derivation does not establish a monotone similarity increase or variance decrease.
key_findings.evidence: The exact variance expansion retains the uncontrolled cross-term 2 n^-1 sum_i (A_is-bar(A_s)) <x_i-bar(x),v_s>. The proof upper-bounds its magnitude by a term proportional to sqrt(Var(A_s)) times the pre-existing centered spread and ||v_s||, then states a looser big-O upper bound. An upper bound by old variance plus nonnegative error cannot imply contraction. In the uniform-broadcast case, the appendix explicitly says centered variance is approximately preserved while a common vector is added. Whether raw cosine similarity rises depends on the mean, vector direction, and norms and is not proved.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the headline Gating + Registers row combines metrics from two different trained architectures despite the stated ImageNet-based variant-selection rule.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix D says Table 1 selects elementwise versus headwise gating by mean ImageNet accuracy. Table 6 makes elementwise + registers the clear selected combined architecture (about 69.36% versus 69.13%). Table 7 shows that Table 1's ADE20K value 0.200±0.006 comes from elementwise + registers, but its VOC12 value 0.524±0.013 comes from headwise + registers; the selected elementwise model is 0.522±0.017 on VOC12. Thus the combined model still leads either task within the reported variants, but the summary row and uncertainty do not describe one model.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the evidence that gating plus registers changes sink phenotypes and the evidence that it improves dense probes come from different training recipes, so the paper does not demonstrate the proposed mechanism-performance link in one model population.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 and Tables 6-7 evaluate 100-epoch self-supervised LeJEPA ViT-L backbones trained with three seeds. Appendix E states that Figure 6 right, used to claim suppression of no-op sinks and redirection of broadcast sinks, instead comes from a separately trained 90-epoch supervised ViT-L/16 model with 76.18% top-1; no seed count, matched supervised baseline, or dense probe is reported for that diagnostic run. Conversely, the LeJEPA models with dense gains are not given the two-axis sink diagnostic. Complementarity in performance is observed, but its attribution to selectively fixing the two diagnosed mechanisms is not directly tested.

anchors.section: Appendix E supervised Figure 6 run and Table 7

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: low stable rank is a sink-geometry consequence, not a mechanism-specific broadcast test, and the pretrained classification remains correlational without payload or causal interventions.
key_findings.evidence: For any nearly perfect sink, Lemma 3 gives O approximately equal to a_s v_s^T and therefore rank at most one, including a no-op sink when v_s is tiny; stable rank is scale-invariant and becomes numerically delicate near the zero matrix. Pairing rank with value norm helps, but a content-scale shared update does not by itself show that the value contains useful image-global information. The pretrained study does not patch, ablate, decode, or counterfactually swap sink payloads to test whether the assigned mode causes model behavior.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the intervention evidence supports complementary architectural benefits in one self-supervised ViT recipe, but does not identify no-op removal and broadcast support as the causal source of those gains.
key_findings.evidence: The controlled performance comparison uses only LeJEPA ViT-L/16, ImageNet-1K pretraining for 100 epochs, three seeds, and frozen linear segmentation probes. Gating and registers change architecture and optimization in multiple ways, and there is no intervention that selectively disables an independently diagnosed no-op or broadcast payload while holding capacity and training dynamics fixed. The null ImageNet result shows that the gain is localized to the evaluated linear dense probes, while the separate supervised diagnostic run cannot causally connect phenotype removal to those LeJEPA gains.

method.core_idea: Treat an attention sink as an ambiguous routing pattern and classify its computation from the residual payload: negligible sink values indicate adaptive suppression, whereas content-scale sink values plus shared low-rank updates are consistent with broadcast.
method.mechanism: The paper proposes residual-payload diagnostics for a single sink-dominated head, constructs separate Gaussian regression tasks requiring conditional suppression or selected-source communication, and measures value norms, query-key spectra, attention inflow, and attention-update stable rank. It applies those diagnostics observationally to pretrained DINOv2, OpenCLIP/CLIP, and EVA ViTs and to register-equipped DINOv2. Six separately trained 100-epoch LeJEPA ViT-L variants span elementwise/headwise gating and four registers; frozen ADE20K/VOC12 linear segmentation probes test patch representations and an online ImageNet classifier is a global-feature control. A distinct 90-epoch supervised ViT-L/16 run supplies the combined gating-plus-register sink-diagnostic plot, so mechanism change and LeJEPA probe improvement are not measured on the same backbones.
assumptions: A sink-dominated single-head approximation isolates the computation despite multi-head output projection, MLPs, residual accumulation, and LayerNorm.
Near-zero sink value norm is sufficient evidence of a no-op contribution rather than cancellation or a downstream use after projection.
Content-scale value norm plus low stable rank identifies useful broadcast rather than a generic outer-product consequence of concentrated attention.
The hand-designed conditional-damping and selected-source regression tasks are faithful minimal models of pretrained sink roles.
The chosen sink detector and normalization make value-norm ratios and stable rank comparable across layers, heads, tokens, and architectures.
Gating mainly supplies conditional no-op capacity, while registers mainly supply a broadcast substrate, despite both changing capacity and optimization.
Linear dense-probe gains reflect improved spatial representations and are not primarily probe selection, capacity, or optimization effects.
Results from ImageNet-trained ViT-L LeJEPA and three pretrained vision families generalize to other data, sizes, objectives, and possibly causal-language settings.
Three independently trained backbones adequately characterize intervention uncertainty.
The separately trained supervised gating-plus-register model is representative of the sink phenotypes in the three-seed LeJEPA intervention models.

techniques.role: Tests whether the dominant attended token carries a negligible or content-scale payload.
Measures whether tokens receive a shared low-dimensional update.
Detects a dominant interaction direction used for conditional routing.
Creates a minimal objective that rewards adaptive suppression of an attention-branch update.
Creates a minimal objective requiring all tokens to retrieve and add one content token.
Projects detected ViT sinks onto value-norm and update-rank axes across layers and heads.
Compares direct output gating, learned workspace tokens, and their combination.
Evaluates spatial information with ADE20K and VOC12 segmentation probes.
Checks whether intervention gains extend to ImageNet online linear classification.

evaluations.setting: Single-head d=64, length-32 Gaussian conditional-damping task trained for roughly 30k AdamW steps (paper pp. 5, 13-14)
evaluations.metric: Sink attention, sink value norm, and singular spectrum of W_Q W_K^T
evaluations.result: Reported runs converge to a dedicated near-zero-value sink and a dominant query-key singular direction; sinks also emerge under partial damping and low no-op frequencies.
evaluations.baseline: A no-sink threshold condition and the analytically possible dispersed cancellation solution, which is not found in the reported runs.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer, one-head d=64, length-32 Gaussian selected-source broadcast task trained for 30k steps (paper pp. 6-7, 14-16)
evaluations.metric: Selected-sink match, sink strength, value/key norms, update uniformity, query similarity, and stable rank
evaluations.result: One layer becomes a source-selecting broadcast hub with content-scale values and update stable rank near one; the second remains more identity-like.
evaluations.baseline: No separately trained alternative architecture; the contrast is the second processing layer and the no-op toy task.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained DINOv2-L/G, OpenCLIP-L/16, OpenAI CLIP-L, and EVA-G vision transformers (paper pp. 7-9, 24-26)
evaluations.metric: Maximum attention inflow, headwise sink frequency, sink-value ratio, and attention-update stable rank
evaluations.result: Plots show an early CLS-to-late-patch handoff, specialized sink heads, and low-value versus content-scale/rank-one modes across the inspected families.
evaluations.baseline: Cross-model qualitative replication; no ground-truth mechanism labels, causal perturbation, seed interval, or diagnostic accuracy metric.

evaluations.setting: Pretrained DINOv2-G with four register tokens (paper pp. 8, 23)
evaluations.metric: Sink-token identity, value-norm ratio, and update stable rank
evaluations.result: Registers capture nearly all displayed sink assignments and populate both the low-value majority mode and a smaller content-scale rank-one mode.
evaluations.baseline: DINOv2-G without registers, where CLS and patches receive the sink assignments.

evaluations.setting: LeJEPA ViT-L/16, ImageNet-1K self-supervised pretraining for 100 epochs, three seeds per variant (paper pp. 9, 21-23)
evaluations.metric: Frozen-backbone ADE20K and Pascal VOC12 linear-probe mIoU
evaluations.baseline: Vanilla LeJEPA backbone plus isolated register and headwise/elementwise gating variants.

evaluations.setting: The same six LeJEPA variants and three seeds (paper pp. 9, 22)
evaluations.result: Means remain tightly clustered: baseline about 69.37%, registers 69.31%, elementwise gating 69.52%, elementwise+registers 69.36%, headwise gating 69.07%, and headwise+registers 69.13%.
evaluations.baseline: Vanilla baseline; this is a reported negative result for broad classification improvement.

evaluations.setting: A separate supervised ViT-L/16 with gating plus four registers, trained on ImageNet-1K for 90 epochs (paper pp. 9, 23)
evaluations.metric: Sink value-norm ratio versus attention-update stable rank and ImageNet top-1
evaluations.result: Figure 6 right is interpreted as suppressing low-value no-op sinks and redirecting content-scale rank-one sinks to registers; Appendix E reports 76.18% top-1.
evaluations.baseline: No matched supervised baseline, independent seed count, numerical cluster summary, or dense probe is reported; this model is not one of the three-seed LeJEPA backbones in Tables 6-7.

limitations: Author-stated: it is unclear when ViT gating benefits arise and whether the effects persist or grow with model, data, and training scale.
Author-stated: gating and registers do not remove useful broadcast sinks, and architectures that support broadcast without sink behavior remain future work.
Reviewer-identified: pretrained mechanism assignments are observational and lack payload decoding, activation patching, targeted ablation, or counterfactual sink swaps.
Reviewer-identified: rank-one output is entailed by sink concentration for either proposed mechanism; stable rank alone is not a broadcast-specific diagnostic and is fragile near zero output.

Reviewer-identified: the increased-similarity lemma supplies neither a variance-contraction result nor a monotone cosine-similarity result; its own uniform case preserves centered variance approximately.
Reviewer-identified: the main Table 1 combined row splices ADE20K and VOC12 results from elementwise and headwise combined variants.
Reviewer-identified: mitigation is evaluated only with ImageNet-trained LeJEPA ViT-L/16 backbones, three seeds, and linear probes; classification does not improve.
Reviewer-identified: the pretrained diagnostic sample covers DINOv2, OpenCLIP/CLIP, and EVA vision encoders but no language model, causal decoder, or non-vision architecture.
Reviewer-identified: toy targets explicitly encode the hypothesized mechanisms and show optimization feasibility, not that naturally trained models use the same algorithms.
Reviewer-identified: gating and registers alter parameterization, capacity, and optimization, so their gains do not causally identify the proposed no-op/broadcast division.
Reviewer-identified: diagnostic plots do not report labeled precision/recall, effect-size uncertainty, input sensitivity, or formal cluster-selection criteria.

Reviewer-identified: the finite-epsilon no-op lemma omits a factor of 1/(1-epsilon_i), does not make the zero-value construction sufficient for arbitrary delta, and treats query-specific cancellation vectors as one shared sink value.
Reviewer-identified: the adaptivity proof establishes only a sufficient rank-one alignment and a product requirement on spectral and sink norms, not the claimed exhaustive two-regime mechanism.

Reviewer-identified: toy experiments do not report independent run counts, seeds, tabulated endpoints, or uncertainty sufficient to support claims that optimization consistently selects the displayed topology.

Reviewer-identified: the sink-mitigation diagnostic uses one separately trained supervised model, whereas dense performance uses three-seed LeJEPA models; neither experiment jointly measures mechanism and performance.

Reviewer-identified: the dense linear-probe architecture, optimizer, schedule, selection protocol, and per-seed results are not documented beyond saying that a single linear segmentation probe is trained on each frozen backbone.

Reviewer-identified: the abstract claims gains in stability, but the intervention study reports token norms and task metrics rather than a defined training-stability outcome such as divergence rate, gradient scale, or sharpness.
failure_modes: A near-zero attention output has undefined or unstable stable rank and is mislabeled as broadcast because the scale diagnostic is omitted or noisy.
A content-scale rank-one update broadcasts a constant, positional artifact, or harmful outlier rather than useful global information.
Multiple sinks, diffuse routing, multi-head cancellation, output projection, or MLP compensation violate the single-sink head approximation.
Value-norm thresholds drift across layers or architectures and turn a continuous spectrum into an artificial two-cluster story.
A common additive payload changes raw cosine similarity in the opposite direction from the claimed effect because of its orientation relative to token means.
Registers absorb attention maps without removing the downstream pathology, or they consume capacity needed by content tokens.
Gating suppresses useful communication because a head classified as no-op is conditionally contentful on rare inputs.
Dense linear-probe gains fail under fine-tuning, detection, retrieval, higher resolution, different pretraining data, or a different self-supervised objective.
A summary table selects the best architecture separately per downstream task while presenting the numbers as one preselected model.
The combined intervention improves optimization generically, making a mechanism-specific causal interpretation appear stronger than the evidence.
Finite-epsilon cancellation differs across queries, so a single learned sink value cannot implement the proof's proposed cancellation simultaneously.
A mechanism plot from a supervised run is implicitly paired with probe gains from different self-supervised runs, creating a false within-model causal narrative.
An apparent dense-probe gain depends on undocumented probe hyperparameters or seed/model selection rather than a better frozen representation.
reusable_insights: Interpret attention jointly with the value payload and residual update; a routing map alone cannot distinguish information use from suppression.
Test both update magnitude and dimensionality because rank is scale-insensitive and a zero-rank limit can mimic a shared outer product numerically.
Use causal payload interventions—patch, zero, swap, or decode the sink value—to establish whether a putative broadcast contains task-relevant global information.
Separate architectural interventions by the computation they make cheap: explicit output gates provide a direct no-op, while workspace tokens provide communication slots.
Include a representation-use control: an intervention can improve localized features while leaving aggregate classification unchanged.
Pre-register one model-selection rule and report every downstream metric for that same selected model; retain a full factorial table for transparency.
Do not infer contraction from an upper bound equal to the old variance plus a nonnegative term; inspect cross-terms and equality cases.
Replicate diagnostic clusters across objectives and architectures, then quantify classification accuracy against ground-truth synthetic interventions before assigning semantic labels.
open_questions: Can sink-value patching or ablation show that the high-value mode causally transmits image-global information?
What statistic distinguishes a useful broadcast from a generic, constant, or harmful low-rank shared update?
Can the token-similarity lemma be replaced with conditions that genuinely imply increased cosine alignment or reduced centered variance?
How stable are the two diagnostic modes across images, resolutions, augmentations, checkpoints, and independently trained seeds?
Do no-op and broadcast modes occur in causal language models under the same diagnostics after accounting for masking?
Does gating plus registers improve dense performance under DINO, MAE, supervised, multimodal, and larger-scale training recipes?
Do gains persist under end-to-end segmentation fine-tuning rather than frozen linear probing?
Can a factorial intervention selectively remove diagnosed no-op sinks or reroute diagnosed broadcasts while holding parameter count and optimization budget fixed?
How should stable rank be defined or thresholded for very small update matrices?
Would multiple dedicated token types or an explicit message-passing primitive support broadcast without concentrating softmax mass?
Which single combined architecture should Table 1 report under its declared ImageNet-selection rule, and do conclusions change after correcting the row?

Can Lemma 1 be repaired with the missing finite-epsilon denominator and a genuinely query-uniform cancellation condition, and can Lemma 2 be weakened to the sufficient product condition it actually proves?
Does a single matched, multi-seed backbone show both the predicted sink-mode change and the dense-representation gain under a preregistered stability and probe protocol?

competitive_landscape.title: Quantizable Transformers: Removing Outliers by Helping Attention Heads Do Nothing
competitive_landscape.difference: Bondarenko et al. argue that softmax attention heads create outliers because they lack a direct no-op and add gated attention to make doing nothing easy. The present paper formalizes near-zero sink values as one of two sink computations, contrasts it with broadcast, and evaluates the combination with registers in ViTs.

competitive_landscape.title: Active-Dormant Attention Heads: Mechanistically Demystifying Extreme-Token Phenomena in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Guo et al. identify active-dormant heads whose extreme tokens absorb attention while value-output norms collapse, directly anticipating the no-op/value-drain interpretation in LLMs. This paper adds an explicit broadcast alternative, controlled two-task signatures, and a ViT intervention study.

competitive_landscape.title: Vision Transformers Need Registers
competitive_landscape.difference: Darcet et al. introduce learned register tokens to absorb high-norm artifacts and improve dense visual features, motivating the workspace/broadcast side of the current framing. The present paper interprets registers as hosts for both contentful broadcast and no-op sinks and combines them with explicit gating.

competitive_landscape.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free
competitive_landscape.difference: Qiu et al. benchmark attention gates at LLM scale and attribute broad gains to nonlinearity, sparsity, and removal of sinks. The present work transports a gating variant to LeJEPA ViTs and gives it a no-op interpretation, but does not isolate that mechanism from the more general effects emphasized by Qiu et al.

competitive_landscape.title: A Unified View of Attention and Residual Sinks: Outlier-Driven Rescaling is Essential for Transformer Training
competitive_landscape.difference: Qiu et al. connect attention and residual sinks through outlier-driven rescaling and argue that the phenomenon can be essential to training. That mechanism is not equivalent to a no-op/broadcast functional split and supplies a competing explanation that the current diagnostic plots do not directly rule out.

competitive_landscape.title: Vision Transformers Don't Need Trained Registers
competitive_landscape.difference: Jiang et al. identify register neurons and construct training-free register tokens that can match trained-register benefits without retraining. This weakens any implication that a learned register architecture is uniquely required for broadcast and suggests a closer capacity-controlled intervention for the current hypothesis.

competitive_landscape.title: Do All Vision Transformers Need Registers? A Cross-Architectural Reassessment
competitive_landscape.difference: This reassessment tests register claims across vision-transformer architectures and sizes and reports that the need and effect are not universal. It sets the missing generalization test for the current single-family LeJEPA mitigation result and cautions against making register complementarity architecture-independent.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a unifying two-algorithm view in which the same attention-sink pattern implements either adaptive no-op or broadcast, derives distinct operational signatures, finds both at scale in pretrained ViTs, and shows that gating plus registers works because the interventions target complementary computations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Separate synthetic objectives recover the intended routing patterns; pretrained ViT plots combine sink-value ratios and update stable rank; register-equipped DINOv2 retains both plotted modes; and three-seed LeJEPA ViT-L experiments show complementary dense linear-probe gains with an unchanged ImageNet control. However, the sink-mitigation plot comes from a separate one-run supervised model rather than those LeJEPA backbones, and the finite-epsilon no-op, adaptivity, and token-similarity arguments overstate what their displayed algebra establishes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the explicit decision framework that asks whether a sink carries a residual payload and the empirical juxtaposition of gating with registers. The no-op component has close mechanistic and gating antecedents, while registers already motivate workspace computation. Low rank is not broadcast-specific, the pretrained assignments lack causal payload tests, and mechanism change and representation gain are not jointly measured in one model. Because the main finite-epsilon dichotomy, adaptivity dichotomy, and similarity conclusions are not established as stated, the theoretical contribution should be treated as a useful hypothesis-and-diagnostic package rather than a validated two-mechanism theorem. The one-family intervention and architecture-spliced headline row further limit the performance claim.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification independently covered all 26 pinned PDF pages, including both toy-model specifications, Lemmas 1-4 and every Appendix B proof, all pretrained-extension figures, LeJEPA architecture/compute details, Tables 1 and 6-7 with every seed, and Appendix E's separate supervised run. Every finding and page anchor was rechecked against the rendered PDF and extracted text; table means were recomputed. The audit corrected three proof overclaims (finite-epsilon no-op, adaptivity dichotomy, and increased similarity), the architecture-spliced Table 1 row, and the evidential mismatch between the supervised mechanism diagnostic and self-supervised dense probes. Low-rank non-identifiability and the missing causal bridge are reviewer inferences from the paper's own outer-product lemma and experiment partition, not author admissions. PDF/text hashes match the indexed pin. Seven nonduplicate primary competitors were checked at their exact current official arXiv revisions on 2026-08-23.
